# `liber:crypto-device@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:crypto-device` package (`crypto-device.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem symmetric crypto offload - the contract a `crypto` provider serves.  A CIPHER ENGINE THE MACHINE OFFERS, AND NOTHING THIS SYSTEM DEPENDS ON. Software cryptography stays the correctness baseline: nothing in the tree routes its own encryption here, and what this contract answers is checked against published vectors and against the software implementation, not trusted for itself. A virtual machine's engine is the HOST'S - it sees every key and every byte - so offloading to it is never safer than doing the work here.  A KEY IS HANDED ONCE AND NEVER ANSWERED BACK. `open` carries it to the device, which keeps it under the session; the driver zeroes its own copy as soon as the device has answered, and no operation returns it. A session belongs to the connection that opened it: another connection naming its number is refused, and every session a connection holds is destroyed when it closes.  EACH REQUEST STANDS ALONE. The IV travels with the data, and nothing carries from one request to the next - so there is no chained state for a host to replay or a migration to lose. Operations whose safety depends on such state are not offered until their threat model is written.

### enum `cipher`

The ciphers this contract can name: AES with a 128-, 192- or 256-bit key, in cipher block chaining - whole 16-byte blocks, with a 16-byte IV. ONE, BECAUSE ONE IS WHAT CAN BE PROVED HERE: QEMU's engine offers CBC alone, and a mode named without an engine to run it against would be a promise nobody has checked.
